newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-June 3.

text.p: There are 28 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- EXPRESS NEWS said that with less than a month to go before the handover, how Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa treated pro-democracy parties and groups will be the centre of concern of Hong Kong people and the international community. Hong Kong people had the responsibility to let Beijing know their real thoughts, and future Hong Kong leaders should often review their own attitudes and keep reminding themselves not to do things which only please Beijing, the paper said.

-- The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO said Tung Chee-hwa's recent media statements were from his heart, reflecting his pride as a Chinese and his confidence towards the implementation of the "one country, two systems" principle. The paper said Tung was right in saying that patriotic Hong Kong people should do things which will make the motherland stronger and more prosperous, and not engage in activities which may split the country and harm national interests.

-- The English-language HONGKONG STANDARD said that since Hong Kong has not traditionally had politicians, civil servants have been involved in formulating policies. Some people were worried that Tung Chee-hwa might in future tend to rely more on outside people for advice. If such misconceptions did exist, the paper said, Tung must clear them up before they had a disastrous effect on morale.
